title: Columbus did not prove the Earth was round.
description:
Columbus did not prove the Earth was round. Educated Europeans already knew it was a sphere. Stephen Jay Gould wrote that there never was a period of flat Earth darkness among scholars.

The dispute was about size. The issue in the 1490s was not the shape of the Earth but its size, and where the east coast of Asia lay.

Columbus shrank the world. He read a figure in Arabic miles as the shorter Italian mile, making his estimate about 25 percent too small.

Columbus's estimate of the distance west to Japan, about 5,000 km. The real distance is roughly four times that.

Spain's advisers said he was wrong. The learned men replied that Columbus had grossly underestimated the distance to Asia.

Washington Irving wrote the scene. His romanticised 1828 biography invented a commission whose ignorant members raised scriptural objections. No first hand record of such objections exists.

The scholars were right about the sums.
